title: Stoplamp Switch Removal and Installation
introduction:
The stoplamp switch sits at the brake-pedal bracket. I use the drawing’s inset to locate it, then the larger view to distinguish the blue switch from its electrical connection. The key to this job is leaving the pedal alone: moving it during removal or installation can upset the switch adjustment. Think of the pedal as a ruler you must not move halfway through a measurement.

I finish the illustrated removal and refit with an ordinary stoplamp check after the switch is fully installed. The pedal stays untouched during service; the check happens only when the assembly and footwell are ready.

items.name: Review the applicable precautions
items.detail: Before beginning, review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). The operations here concern the pedal-mounted electrical switch; they do not require brake-fluid handling or friction-component work.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service around the vehicle. Otherwise, remote starting could occur at any time and cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use the applicable protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Keep the car stationary
items.detail: Park the vehicle and apply the parking brake. Leave it on the ground throughout this switch operation.

edits.text: NOTICE: Leave the brake pedal untouched while removing or installing the stoplamp switch. Pressing or pulling the pedal during either operation can misadjust or damage the switch.
edits.why: The pedal position is the reference for this work. Keeping it stationary protects the switch’s adjustment as well as the component itself.

edits.text: Remove the stoplamp switch from the brake-pedal bracket using the connector-disconnection and rotation steps below.
edits.why: The inset locates the switch in the pedal assembly, while the larger view identifies the target component in blue. Match that location before disturbing a nearby connection.

edits.text: Unplug the electrical connector from the stoplamp switch.
edits.why: The magenta-highlighted connection is the electrical attachment to separate before turning the switch. This leaves the wiring free of the switch’s removal movement.

edits.text: Rotate the stoplamp switch clockwise to release it, then remove it from its mounting.
edits.why: The switch releases by rotation. Keep the brake pedal stationary throughout this movement.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: position the stoplamp switch in its mounting, turn it counterclockwise to secure it, then reconnect its electrical connector. Keep the brake pedal untouched throughout installation.
edits.why:
Reversing the sequence secures the switch before restoring its electrical connection. The pedal-position notice applies during refitting just as it does during removal.

Only after the switch is fully fitted and its connector latched, clear tools and your hands from the footwell. With the vehicle parked and parking brake applied, press and release the brake pedal while a helper observes both rear stoplamps and the high-mounted stoplamp. Confirm they illuminate while the pedal is pressed and go out after release. This ordinary completion check follows the lamp behavior described in the [exterior lighting overview](#/document/G1694241); it does not isolate a defective circuit component. Resolve any incorrect lamp behavior before driving.

operationalClarification.basis: Ordinary completion check, not Ford fault isolation, consistent with independently reviewed same-source workshop counterpart.
